peigneur.text: Imagine working on an oil rig... when the entire lake beneath you starts disappearing.
The water begins to spin. And the rig starts to tilt.
This is Lake Peigneur, in Louisiana. November twentieth, nineteen eighty.
The lake was only ten feet deep. But beneath it was a giant salt mine.
That morning, an oil drill got stuck more than twelve hundred feet down.
It had punched straight into the mine.
Water poured in, dissolving the salt pillars that held the tunnels up.
The hole grew wider... and the lake drained, like a giant bathtub.
A whirlpool swallowed the rig, a tugboat, eleven barges, and part of an island.
Even a nearby canal flowed backwards, into a hundred-and-sixty-foot waterfall.
All seven men on the rig escaped. So did all fifty-five miners.
Nobody was killed. But when the lake refilled... it was salt water.
